newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH CHIEF ATTACKS SOUTH AFRICAN "BIGHEADS".
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH CHIEF ATTACKS SOUTH AFRICAN "BIGHEADS".

text.p: French rugby union chief Bernard Lapasset has called South Africa "bigheads" as the Springboks prepare to tour France.

The French daily newspaper Parisien reported on Friday that the South African tour management had been making outrageous demands for their visit, while French Rugby Federation (FFR) president Lapasset responded by accusing the Springboks of becoming "bigheads".

According to Parisien, the Springbok team management had requested specific recreational facilities in their hotels, two international lawyers to be available for each of their tour matches in Bordeaux, Brive, Lyon and Paris while, at the same time, declining to attend certain post-match functions.
South Africa had refused to attend two gala banquets after the test matches in Bordeaux and Paris, the newspaper reported.

"This is inexplicable. It is the height of bad manners. It is also a snub to French Prime Minister Alain Juppe who, as Mayor of Bordeaux, was scheduled to attend the test match and the banquet afterwards," an FFR spokesman said.
Lapasset was fuming at what he termed "outrageous demands by the Springboks for their tour", the newspaper said.

"The Springbok officials have short memories. During their period of isolation, they were only too glad to have the support of (former FFR president) Albert Ferrasse. They ought to show gratitude instead of insulting us. But presumably now they are world champions, they have become bigheads," Lapasset said.
The South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) response on Saturday was conciliatory.

"The Springbok team and SARFU certainly do not wish to cause any offence to the French Rugby Federation and I shall discuss this matter further with Mr Lapasset to eliminate any misunderstandings," SARFU media officer Alex Broun said.

"Andre Markgraaff and his assistant tour manager Koos de Beer visited France recently, examined all the facilities and hotels and felt that the arrangements made were excellent. But there was a large number of proposed events, some of which they felt he team would not be able to attend."
Broun said some of the arrangements for the Springbok team were in addition to what the FFR initially provided but that SARFU was financing these extra arrangements.
"This is similar to what happened when the New Zealand team toured South Africa earlier this year -- a tour, I would point out, that was extremely successful for them.

"As for the recreational facilities in the hotels, these are standard for most touring teams and as for not attending certain functions, the Springbok manager Andre Markgraaff believes on such a long tour the players can't attend everything."
